# Check that go line in go.work is always >= go line of used modules.

# A version below the used module's go line fails during module loading.
# The error names the version the module wants. Raising the go.work line to
# it needs a go command that is at least that version, so this is a
# misconfigured system that should not arise in practice.
env TESTGO_VERSION=go1.21.1
cp go.work go.work.orig
! go list
stderr '^go: module . listed in go.work file requires go >= 1.21.2, but go.work lists go 1.21.1; to use go 1.21.2:\n\tgo work use$'

# Using a new enough Go version, fails later and can suggest 'go work use'.
env TESTGO_VERSION=go1.21.2
cp go.work.orig go.work
! go list
stderr '^go: module . listed in go.work file requires go >= 1.21.2, but go.work lists go 1.21.1; to use go 1.21.2:\n\tgo work use$'

# go work use fixes the problem.
go work use
go list

-- go.work --
go 1.21.1
use .

-- go.mod --
module m
go 1.21.2

-- p.go --
package p
